newsitem.title: USA: Ortho Centers sees Q3 at least $0.09/shr.
newsitem.headline: Ortho Centers sees Q3 at least $0.09/shr.

text.p: Orthodontic Centers of America Inc said Monday it expects to report third quarter earnings of at least $0.09 per share, noting this is at or above analysts' expectations.
The company also said it had revenues of between $18.5 and $19.5 million in the latest quarter, noting these are within the range of analysts' expectations.

Orthodontic Centers said it believes the unusual trading activity in the company's common stock on October 11 may be attributable to rumors stemming from an analyst's comment that third quarter net revenues would be below market expectations.
In trading Friday, Orthodontic Centers' stock dropped 4-5/8 to 12-3/4 on volume of nearly 3.7 million shares.
The company also cited a comment in the November issue of Worth magazine regarding its accounting for Friday's activity.

Chief executive Gasper Lazzara Jr said, "We believe Orthodontic Centers of America maintains its financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and comments in Worth magazine regarding its financial statement presentation are unfounded."

Noting final third quarter and nine months results will be reported on October 31, he said "we expect to report net revenues between $18.5 million and $19.5 million for the third quarter, and we believe these estimates are within the range of market expectations. Finally, the company expects to report earnings per share of at least $0.09, which are at or above analyst expectations."

The First Call consensus estimate for Orthodontic Centers' latest quarter is $0.09 per share, and $0.10 for the fourth quarter. The service compares this with $0.12 and $0.13 per share, respectively, in 1995.

During the third quarter, Orthodontic Centers opened 37 new centers (21 newly developed and 16 affiliations with existing practices), the company said. After consolidations, the company ended the quarter with 189 offices in 26 states. Further, the number of orthodontists affiliating with the company during the third quarter was a net of 22, bringing the total number of orthodontists with the company to 108 as of September 30.

Lazzara commented, "We are very pleased with our preliminary results. We attribute our record financial performance to the accelerated number of doctor affiliations and new center openings during the second half of the year. ...Given the number of pending affiliations and the strong acquisition pipeline, we expect record results for the fourth quarter and for 1997."
